subject: Proposed time-slicing for demos to cover US/EU/APAC holidays
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan@brighthealth.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: engops@brighthealth.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800 (PST)
Subject: Re: Demo — need flexible windows for global attendees

Hi Neha / Aditya,

Thanks for the quick follow-up after the intro call. We're excited to see Redwood in action. Before we lock a single 60–75 minute slot, a couple of constraints from our side:

- Our engineering leadership in Tokyo will be mostly out for Golden Week (11/3–11/10 JST) and some extended OOO into the week after — they asked to avoid early-morning JST slots that fall into their holiday catch-up.
- Our India product lead will be observing Diwali family travel on 11/12–11/14 IST and prefers no evening IST slots on those dates.
- UK/EU attendees have public bank holiday coverage changes around the second week of November (Easter-like project calendar shift); they prefer late-morning UK time.

We realize this is messy across US/EU/APAC + recent DST shifts. Two asks:
1) Could Redwood propose an alternative that doesn't require one long continuous meeting for all regions?
2) We prefer options that keep each regional group in short focused blocks and still leave time for cross-region Q&A.

Would appreciate a couple of concrete options with timezone conversions — we can then confirm attendees.

Best,
Susan Park
Sr. Product Ops, BrightHealth Analytics

---

On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 09:05 AM PST Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:

> Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800 (PST)
> Subject: RE: Demo — need flexible windows for global attendees
>
> Hi Susan — thanks for the detail, that helps.
>
> We can absolutely avoid a single long meeting and instead propose a "time-slicing" approach: three short regional demo blocks (30 minutes each) + a final 20-minute global wrap/Q&A that is recorded for people who can't join live. Two concrete options below (all times shown with conversions):
>
> Option A — Staggered live + global wrap (we repeat a 15–20 minute feature walk for US/EU/APAC attendees)
> - Block 1 (APAC focus): 08:00–08:30 JST / 04:00–04:30 IST / 19:00–19:30 PST (previous day)
> - Block 2 (EMEA focus): 10:30–11:00 CET / 14:30–15:00 IST / 01:30–02:00 PST
> - Block 3 (Americas focus): 10:00–10:30 PST / 13:00–13:30 EST / 18:00–18:30 UTC
> - Global wrap (recorded): 17:00 UTC / 12:00 PST / 18:00 CET — 20 min Q&A (optional for APAC)
>
> Option B — Time-slicing (short, sequential regional deep-dives + overlapping handoff) — reduces duplicate content and keeps each session highly targeted
> - APAC deep-dive: 06:30–07:00 JST / 03:00–03:30 IST / 14:30–15:00 PST (previous day)
> - Handoff window (internal only): 15:00–15:30 PST (engineering sync + buffer)
> - Americas live: 10:00–10:30 PST / 13:00–13:30 EST
> - EMEA office hours: 17:00–17:30 CET / 16:00–16:30 GMT (recorded)
>
> Notes and constraints: we will avoid 11/12 evening IST (per your Diwali note) and avoid 11/3–11/10 morning JST where possible. Because of DST shifts, our automatic conversions include UTC as the anchor; we'll send calendar invites in UTC and local-time strings.
>
> I've attached a short agenda (demo-agenda-v2.pdf) and a mutual-action plan (MAP-redwood-brighthealth.xlsx) with proposed owners for follow-ups. If you prefer, we can also schedule two of the blocks on different days (e.g., APAC block one day earlier) — just tell us which attendees are must-have.
>
> Quick ask: which option feels best for your team (A = repeat/minimize cross-region attendance, B = focused slices + handoff)?
>
> Thanks,
> Neha Kapoor
> Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
>
> Office: +1-415-555-0199
>
>
